title: Top 10 Water Parks in Thailand for Families 2026 — Splash, Slide & Soak
excerpt: Thailand's water parks have gone next-level. From enormous wave pools in Pattaya to jungle-themed slides in Phuket and lazy rivers in Bangkok, here's our guide to the best family water parks across Thailand in 2026.
content:
Thailand's tropical climate makes water parks an essential part of any family itinerary. The good news: the country has invested heavily in world-class water attractions — there are now over 20 major water parks across the kingdom, and the best ones rival anything in Singapore, Dubai, or the United States. We spent the last six months visiting water parks across Thailand with kids aged 3–12 to bring you this definitive guide.

1. Ramayana Water Park — Pattaya

Best for: Ages 4+ | Location: Na Jomtien, Pattaya | Duration: Full day | Price: 1,190 THB adult / 890 THB child ($33 / $25 USD)

Ramayana is Thailand's largest water park — and it's a stunner. Set on 30 acres of landscaped grounds with views of the Gulf of Thailand, Ramayana features 21 distinct water slides, a massive wave pool that generates 4-metre waves, a 600-metre lazy river, and Thailand's longest aquatic roller coaster (the 'Aqualoop'). The park is themed around the Ramayana epic, with Thai-inspired architecture, lush gardens, and a giant golden demon statue that kids find endlessly entertaining.

The slide lineup is exceptional: the 'Boomerango' sends riders up a near-vertical wall before dropping back down; the 'Aqualoop' features a 360-degree loop enclosed in a translucent tube; the 'Mat Racer' lets four riders race head-first head-to-head on mats; and the 'Python' is a high-speed body slide with unexpected drops. For younger kids, the 'Wave Runner' zone has 12 mini slides, a splash pad, and a kiddie pool with gentle waves.

The park is immaculately clean, lifeguards are everywhere (and actually watching the water), and there are plenty of shaded lounger areas. The food court is decent — think pad thai, fried rice, burgers, and pizza — with prices comparable to Bangkok mall food courts (150–250 THB per dish). Free lockers are included in the ticket price, and towels are available for rent.

Parent verdict: 'Ramayana is worth the trip to Pattaya alone. We spent seven hours here and our 5- and 8-year-old never got bored. The lazy river was my favourite — just floating with a drink while the kids splashed around in the wave pool. The park is cleaner and less crowded than Cartoon Network Amazone.' — James, father of two, Hong Kong.

Parent tip: Book tickets on Klook (about 30% off walk-up prices with hotel transfer included). Arrive at opening time (10am) to claim the best loungers — the shaded ones near the wave pool go first. Water shoes are highly recommended (the concrete paths get scorching by midday). The park allows outside food and drink, though coolers aren't permitted. Thursday and Friday are the quietest days. Bring reef-safe sunscreen — the park sells it but at a premium.

2. Cartoon Network Amazone — Pattaya

Best for: Ages 3–12 (especially Cartoon Network fans) | Location: Bang Saray, Pattaya | Duration: Full day | Price: 1,590 THB adult / 1,190 THB child ($44 / $33 USD)

Cartoon Network Amazone is Thailand's most famous water park — and with good reason. The world's first Cartoon Network-themed water park is packed with slides, rides, and attractions themed around Adventure Time, The Powerpuff Girls, Ben 10, and Gumball. The centrepiece is the 'Omniverse' — a massive multi-level water play structure with over 150 water features, giant tipping buckets, and eight slides of varying intensity.

The park's standout attraction is 'Goop Generator' — a funnel slide that drops riders into a giant toilet bowl before flushing them out. 'Adventure Time River' is a 450-metre lazy river with water features, spray jets, and Cartoon Network character statues. The 'Ben 10 Ultimate Wave' pool generates waves up to 1.5 metres — tame enough for kids but fun for adults too. The 'Powerpuff Girls Splash Pad' is a dedicated zone for younger kids with mini slides, spray guns, and shallow water.

Kid-approved: 'I saw Finn and Jake walking around and got a high-five from Jake! The big water bucket dumped water on my dad and he screamed. Best day ever.' — Emma, age 6, UK.

Parent tip: Cartoon Network Amazone is the priciest water park on this list, but the character interaction (costumed characters roam the park hourly) makes it a treat for young Cartoon Network fans. Check the Klook app for package deals that include lunch vouchers. The park gets extremely crowded on weekends and Thai public holidays — aim for a weekday visit. Parking is free and ample.

3. Vana Nava Water Jungle — Hua Hin

Best for: Ages 5+ (thrill seekers) | Location: Hua Hin | Duration: Full day | Price: 1,200 THB adult / 950 THB child ($33 / $26 USD)

Vana Nava is Thailand's first 'water jungle' — a lush, tropically-themed water park built into a natural hillside overlooking the Gulf of Thailand. The park is divided into two areas: the 'Water Jungle' (the main water park) and the 'Adventure Zone' (a high-ropes course, rock climbing wall, and zip line). The water park's signature attraction is 'The Abyss' — a six-lane mat-racing slide that's one of the longest in Asia at 215 metres. There's also 'The Water Loop' (a 360-degree looping slide), 'Boomerang' (a funnel slide), and 'Free Fall' (a trapdoor drop slide — one of only a handful in Southeast Asia).

The kids' zone, 'Little Jungle,' is excellent — a dedicated area with 10 mini slides, a pirate ship with water cannons, a shallow splash pool, and a smaller version of the lazy river. The 'Lazy River' itself is 370 metres long and winds through the park's lush tropical landscaping — expect to see monitor lizards sunbathing on the banks (they're harmless, just part of the scenery).

Parent tip: Vana Nava is part of the Holiday Inn Resort Vana Nava — hotel guests get free entry. If you're not staying there, book via Klook for the best rates. The park's location on a hillside means lots of stairs — not ideal for prams (though there's a shuttle tram). Bring insect repellent. The Abyss slide requires a minimum height of 107cm. Weekdays are significantly quieter than weekends.

4. Siam Park City — Bangkok

Best for: All ages | Location: Khan Na Yao, East Bangkok | Duration: Full day | Price: 800 THB adult / 500 THB child ($22 / $14 USD)

Siam Park City is Bangkok's original mega water park — it's been around for decades but has undergone a massive renovation that brought it into the 21st century. The park is enormous (over 120 acres) and includes both a water park and a full amusement park with roller coasters, a Ferris wheel, and a giant drop tower. The water park section, 'Siam Water Park,' features Thailand's largest wave pool ('The Super Pool' — 13,000 square metres with waves up to 4 metres), a 750-metre lazy river, and over 20 slides.

The new-for-2025 slides include 'The Twister' (a high-speed funnel slide), 'The Racer' (a 6-lane mat racer), and 'The Spiral' (a 150-metre tube slide with LED light effects). The kids' zone, 'Little World,' is a colourful, fenced area with mini slides, water spray features, and a shallow pool staffed by dedicated lifeguards. The amusement park rides are extra but a family wristband (available at the gate) covers both sections.

Parent verdict: 'Siam Park City is incredible value. We paid 800 baht each and spent 8 hours — the kids did the water slides, the wave pool, the lazy river, AND the amusement park rides. The food is cheap (100 baht for a massive plate of pad thai) and the park is clean. It's a bit far from central Bangkok but worth the trip.' — Maria, mother of three, Philippines.

Parent tip: Siam Park City is a 30-minute drive from central Bangkok (avoid rush hour). The park's biggest weakness is limited shade — bring hats and sunscreen, and consider renting a private cabin (500 THB) for air-conditioned refuge. The amusement park rides are dated but perfectly safe. The park is noticeably quieter Monday–Wednesday. Water shoes are essential — the concrete bakes in Bangkok's sun.

5. Andamanda Water Park — Phuket

Best for: Ages 5+ | Location: Kathu, Phuket | Duration: Full day | Price: 1,400 THB adult / 950 THB child ($39 / $26 USD)

Phuket's newest and largest water park, Andamanda, is a visual spectacle. The park is themed around Thai mythology and the Andaman Sea, with five themed zones: 'Nagara' (the main pool area with a giant wave pool), 'Naga's Lair' (thrill slides), 'White Beach' (a lazy river with a beach-entry pool), 'Vana' (kids' area), and 'Suvarnabhumi' (a golden palace-themed entrance area with restaurants and shops).

The standout slide is 'Python' — Thailand's longest water slide at 380 metres, twisting through the jungle canopy. 'Boomerang' is a funnel slide that reaches near-vertical angles. 'Aqua Loop' is a 360-degree looping slide. The wave pool ('Nagara' wave pool) is enormous and generates waves up to 3 metres — kids aged 5+ with life vests can enjoy the shallower end. The kids' zone ('Vana') is a fantasy-themed area with mini slides, spray cannons, tipping buckets, and a shallow pool with life-sized mythical creature statues.

Kid-approved: 'The Python was so fast! We went through the jungle and I saw birds flying next to us. The wave pool was fun too — I pretended I was surfing.' — Ethan, age 8, Singapore.

Parent tip: Book online via Klook for a 20–30% discount. The park is less crowded than you'd expect for Phuket — the 1,400 baht ticket price filters out budget travellers (though Klook deals bring it closer to 1,000 baht). The food is surprisingly good — the Thai restaurant near the wave pool does an excellent pad kra pao (250 THB). The park has plenty of shaded loungers but they go fast. Arrive at 10am opening to secure a good spot.

6-10. Quick Look at Other Notable Parks

6. Santorini Water Park — Cha-Am

A Greek island-themed water park with white-and-blue architecture, 12 slides, and a wave pool. More affordable (600–800 THB) and less crowded than Hua Hin's Vana Nava. Ideal for families with younger kids who want a half-day option.

7. Black Mountain Water Park — Hua Hin

Part of the Black Mountain Golf Resort, this small but perfectly formed water park has a wave pool, slides, and a kids' zone. The draw is the setting — surrounded by mountains and eucalyptus trees. Free for resort guests; 700 THB for external visitors.

8. Jumpa Water Park — Khao Yai

Khao Yai's first water park, set in the foothills of Khao Yai National Park. The setting is stunning (mountain views from the wave pool), and the kids' zone is excellent. Smaller than the mega-parks but the cool mountain air makes for a more comfortable experience.

9. Carnival Magic — Pattaya

A unique carnival + water park hybrid. The 'Rainbow' water zone has slides, a wave pool, and a lazy river, while the carnival section has rides, games, and a nightly parade. The combination makes it a good choice for families who want variety in one location.

10. Blue Tree Lagoon — Phuket

Not a traditional water park — Blue Tree is a crystal-blue lagoon surrounded by water slides, trampolines, zip lines, and a massive inflatable obstacle course. The vibe is more 'mountain resort meets adventure park' and the natural setting is breathtaking.

Quick Comparison

  • Best overall: Ramayana Water Park (Pattaya) — largest, cleanest, best value for money
  • Best for young kids: Siam Park City (Bangkok) — affordable, kiddie zone, mix with amusement park
  • Best for thrill seekers: Vana Nava (Hua Hin) — trapdoor drop slide, longest mat racer in Asia
  • Best for character-loving kids: Cartoon Network Amazone (Pattaya) — premium but unforgettable
  • Best setting: Andamanda (Phuket) — Thai mythology theme, jungle vistas
  • Best value: Siam Park City (Bangkok) — 800 THB for water park + amusement park
  • Best new addition: Blue Tree Lagoon (Phuket) — natural lagoon, adventure vibes

Practical Tips

  • Book via Klook: Almost every water park in Thailand offers 20–40% discounts through Klook. The discount often includes round-trip hotel transfer — especially useful for Pattaya parks.
  • Go on weekdays: Thai water parks are dramatically quieter Tuesday–Thursday. You'll spend more time sliding and less time queuing.
  • Water shoes are essential: Every reviewer mentions this. The concrete paths get hot enough to burn bare feet by 11am. Buy a pair at Decathlon for 250 THB before your trip.
  • Reef-safe sunscreen: Thailand has banned sunscreens containing oxybenzone, octinoxate, and other reef-harming chemicals. Bring reef-safe sunscreen from home or buy at 7-Eleven (look for the 'Reef Safe' label).
  • Bring a waterproof pouch: A dry bag or waterproof phone pouch is essential for the lazy river and wave pool. Available at any water park gift shop or 7-Eleven for 100–200 THB.
  • Set a meeting point: Water parks are chaotic and phones can't go on most slides. Pick a central meeting point (a specific flagpole, lounge chair number, or food stall) and make sure everyone knows where it is.

Our verdict: Thailand's water park scene has never been stronger. Ramayana Water Park in Pattaya is our top pick for most families — it's the largest, cleanest, and best value of the mega-parks. For Bangkok families who don't want to travel far, Siam Park City offers incredible value at 800 THB including the amusement park. And if you're in Phuket, Andamanda is worth every baht for the setting alone. Whichever park you choose, the one constant is fun — Thailand's water parks have figured out how to make every member of the family happy.
author: Kids Activities Asia Team
